definitions.gloss: hot spring cure; therapeutic bathing at a hot spring
definitions.explanation: The practice of staying at a hot spring for an extended period to treat illness or promote health. A traditional Japanese form of convalescence.

examples.japanese: {温泉|おんせん}で{湯治|とうじ}する。
examples.english: To take a hot spring cure.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎年|まいとし}{湯治|とうじ}に{行|い}っている。
examples.english: My grandmother goes for a hot spring cure every year.

examples.japanese: {湯治|とうじ}{場|ば}として{有名|ゆうめい}なこの{温泉|おんせん}には{長期|ちょうき}{滞在|たいざい}の{客|きゃく}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This hot spring, famous as a therapeutic bathing destination, has many long-term guests.

notes:
{湯治|とうじ} is the traditional practice of staying at a hot spring for an extended period to treat illness or restore health.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- A practice with centuries of history in Japan: people would stay for days or weeks at therapeutic {温泉|おんせん} resorts to recover from chronic ailments, rheumatism, skin conditions, or general fatigue.
- Famous {湯治|とうじ} towns include {草津|くさつ} (Gunma), {鳴子|なるこ} (Miyagi), and {四万|しま} (Gunma).
- Modern day-trip hot-spring visits are not {湯治|とうじ}; the term specifically implies extended stays for health purposes.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {湯治|とうじ}に{行|い}く (to go for a hot-spring cure)
- {湯治|とうじ}{場|ば}: a therapeutic hot-spring resort
- {湯治|とうじ}{客|きゃく}: a guest who stays for a hot-spring cure
- {湯治|とうじ}{宿|やど}: an inn that caters to long-term therapeutic guests

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {温泉|おんせん}{療法|りょうほう}: hot-spring therapy (the modern medical term).
- {温泉|おんせん}{旅行|りょこう}: a regular hot-spring trip (not therapeutic).
- Note the homophones {冬至|とうじ} (winter solstice) and {当時|とうじ} (at that time), which are written with different kanji.
